answer: Each identity must complete a continuous sequence of modular squarings, with each step depending on the previous one; a Wesolowski proof lets others verify the result efficiently but does not remove the prover’s sequential work. An attacker may run clone chains on separate GPUs, but cannot parallelize the steps within any chain to beat its physical time bound. The inlet admits only completed proofs, the vault protects verified identities, and the terrace offers no shortcut around elapsed computation.
